title: "Metrics"

---

## Sign conventions

Two, and they are the single most misread thing here. Both are signed on
purpose: an absolute value merges a track that started *early* with one that
started *late*, which are opposite conditions.

| Quantity | Definition | Good when |
|---|---|---|
| `off_s` | `trk_start − ATOT` | **negative** — the track began before wheels-off, so a receiver heard the aircraft on the ground |
| `land_s` | `trk_end − ALDT` | **positive** — the track ran on past touchdown, through taxi-in |

## Tiers

An aerodrome is in exactly one tier, decided by **its own** measured share —
`measured_pct`, the percentage of movements on its busier side carrying APDF
milestones. Tier A is `measured_pct ≥ 50`.

| Tier | Milestones | Capture metrics | Ranked on |
|---|---|---|---|
| **A** | AOBT, ATOT, ALDT, AIBT — all measured by APDF | yes | `coverage_index` |
| **B** | take-off inferred as `AOBT_3 + TAXI_TIME_3`, landing from `ARVT_3` | **no** — there is no in-block time outside APDF | `detection_pct` |

::: {.callout-note}
## Why the tier is not `t_source`

A flight's `t_source` is `"apdf"` only when **both** of its ends are covered.
That is the right rule for a metric needing both, and the wrong one for a
statistic cut by aerodrome.

Measured on the 2025 sample: 44,841 flights carry a genuine APDF in-block time,
but only 22,588 are labelled `"apdf"` — the other 22,254 *departed* from an
aerodrome APDF does not cover. Tiering on that label put **26 aerodromes with
20 or more movements into the wrong tier despite 99–100% of their arrivals
being measured**, Helsinki and Stuttgart among them, because most of their
traffic arrives from uncovered aerodromes. They would have been ranked on
detection alone with every capture column blank.

The per-endpoint flags `dep_measured` and `arr_measured` carry the answer, and
`t_source` is left untouched so that nothing already published on it moves.
:::

Tier B's inference was validated against real APDF movements at median error
0 s, IQR 17 s (take-off) and 25 s (landing). The tiers are ranked separately
and never interleaved, because they do not measure the same thing.

## Columns

Side-specific columns carry a `_dep` or `_arr` suffix where both sides define
them. Departures group on `gt_adep`, arrivals on `gt_ades`.

### Counts and detection

| Column | Formula | Unit | Domain | Reading |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `n_gt_dep`, `n_gt_arr` | ground-truth movements at this aerodrome | flights | ≥ 0 | sample size; every other column is unreliable when this is small. Ranking requires ≥ 20 |
| `n_detected_dep`, `n_detected_arr` | movements with ≥ 1 assigned state vector | flights | `0..n_gt` | |
| `detection_pct_dep`, `detection_pct_arr` | `100 · n_detected / n_gt` | % | `0..100` | 100 = every movement seen at least once. The most basic coverage reading there is |
| `n_capture_excluded_dep`, `..._arr` | **measured** movements with `AOBT ≥ ATOT` or `AIBT ≤ ALDT` | flights | ≥ 0 | bad reference data, excluded from capture rather than clipped. An *unmeasured* endpoint is not counted here — it has no capture, which is not the same as an impossible one |
| `measured_pct_dep`, `..._arr` | `100 · #(endpoint measured by APDF) / n_gt` | % | `0..100` | decides the tier; `≥ 50` on either side is Tier A |
| `dep_measured`, `arr_measured` | per flight: did APDF supply this endpoint's milestones | bool | — | capture is computed only where true, so a predicted taxi time never becomes a denominator |

`n_gt` counts **all** ground-truth movements while every percentile below is
over **detected** flights only. The asymmetry is deliberate: an undetected
flight has no offset, and the only way to include it in a percentile would be
to invent one.

### Boundary error

| Column | Formula | Unit | Domain | Reading |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `off_s_p10` … `off_s_p90` | percentiles of `off_s` over detected departures | s | signed | `p90` is the worst-covered decile. A `p50` near zero means the typical track starts at wheels-off — no ground reception |
| `land_s_p10` … `land_s_p90` | percentiles of `land_s` over detected arrivals | s | signed | `p10` is the worst-covered decile |
| `off_abs_p50`, `off_abs_p90` | percentiles of `|off_s|` | s | ≥ 0 | **comparability with the V1 study only.** Do not read as coverage: it merges early and late starts |
| `land_abs_p50`, `land_abs_p90` | percentiles of `|land_s|` | s | ≥ 0 | as above |

### Ground capture — Tier A only

Raw seconds are not comparable between aerodromes. A median `off_s` of −180 s
is complete coverage at a regional field with a three-minute taxi and about a
seventh of it at a hub with a twenty-minute one. Normalising by the aerodrome's
own ground phase removes that.

| Column | Formula | Unit | Domain | Reading |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `dep_capture_p10` … `p90` | percentiles of `clip((ATOT − trk_start) / (ATOT − AOBT), 0, 1)`, over `dep_measured` flights only | fraction | `0..1` | share of the taxi-out actually seen |
| `arr_capture_p10` … `p90` | percentiles of `clip((trk_end − ALDT) / (AIBT − ALDT), 0, 1)`, over `arr_measured` flights only | fraction | `0..1` | share of the taxi-in actually seen |
| `dep_no_ground_pct` | `100 · #(off_s ≥ 0) / n_detected` | % | `0..100` | share never heard on the ground at all |
| `arr_no_ground_pct` | `100 · #(land_s ≤ 0) / n_detected` | % | `0..100` | share lost at or before touchdown |
| `dep_full_capture_pct` | `100 · #(dep_capture ≥ 0.95) / n_detected` | % | `0..100` | share whose whole taxi-out was seen |
| `arr_full_capture_pct` | `100 · #(arr_capture ≥ 0.95) / n_detected` | % | `0..100` | |
| `taxi_out_median_s` | median `ATOT − AOBT` | s | > 0 | context: why raw seconds differ between aerodromes |
| `taxi_in_median_s` | median `AIBT − ALDT` | s | > 0 | context |

Capture is computed **only from measured milestones**. Outside APDF the
denominator would be `TAXI_TIME_3`, NM's *predicted* taxi time, so the fraction
would measure the prediction as much as the reception — and mixing predicted
and measured denominators inside one column makes the ranking incomparable with
itself.

A non-positive ground phase — off-block after take-off, in-block before
landing — is bad reference data, not zero coverage. Those flights are
**excluded** from the capture statistics and counted in `n_capture_excluded`.
Clipping them instead would score them 0 or 1 and silently move the median.

### Segmentation quality

Present so a poor coverage number can be attributed to reception or to the
algorithm rather than guessed at. Every flight falls in exactly one class, and
a flight that is both merged and fragmented counts as **merged** — merging is
the worse failure, and a flight must not improve its class by breaking a second
way.

| Column | Formula | Unit | Domain | Reading |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `clean_pct_dep`, `clean_pct_arr` | `100 · #(one flight ↔ one track) / n_gt` | % | `0..100` | |
| `fragmented_pct_dep`, `..._arr` | `100 · #(one flight → several tracks) / n_gt` | % | `0..100` | recoverable downstream — the flight is present in pieces |
| `merged_pct_dep`, `..._arr` | `100 · #(several flights → one track) / n_gt` | % | `0..100` | **unrecoverable** — the other flights simply do not exist in the output |

### The ranking

| Column | Formula | Unit | Domain | Reading |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `coverage_index` | `detection_rate · mean(dep_capture_p50, arr_capture_p50)` | fraction | `0..1` | the expected share of a movement actually captured: the chance it is seen at all, times how much of its ground phase is seen when it is |
| `rank` | position within the tier | — | ≥ 1 | Tier A ranks on `coverage_index`, Tier B on `detection_pct` |

`coverage_index` is **NaN**, not zero, when no capture term exists. A Tier B
aerodrome has no AIBT, and giving it a fabricated capture — zero included —
would rank it below every measured aerodrome for a reason that has nothing to
do with coverage.

Every component stays a visible column so the ranking can be reproduced, or
rejected, on whichever term the reader cares about.
